transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello, Mrs. Al-Rashid. Thank you for meeting with me.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Hello, doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I need to tell you about a mistake with your medicine.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. Three days ago, I wrote in your chart to stop the blood pressure pill. But I did not tell the pharmacy.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Because I did not tell them, the pharmacy kept giving you the pill. You took a medicine that you should not have taken for three days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I... I took it because you said.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Do you understand what I mean? That you took a pill you were supposed to stop?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. I understand.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for this confusion. We were very busy on that day, and it was missed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is okay, doctor. You are the expert.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry. It should not have happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am just... I am surprised. Is it dangerous?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is not dangerous for you right now, but it was a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not know what to do. I trust you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you trust me, and I feel bad that this happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My heart is beating fast. I feel... strange.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I see. It is a lot to hear at once.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just follow the rules. I do not want to cause trouble.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You are not causing any trouble. This was my mistake, not yours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will I be okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. But I want to make sure we are safe now. To be sure I explained this well, can you tell me what happened with the medicine?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You forget to tell the pharmacy. I take the pill for three days too many.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is exactly right.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did this happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I missed a step in the process. I am very sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I see.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Now, here is what we will do to fix this. First, I have already called the pharmacy. They have stopped that medicine now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Second, I want you to look at your pills today. If you see any left of that old medicine, please throw them in the trash. Can you do that for me?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, I can do that today.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Thank you. Third, I am going to check your blood pressure again in one hour to make sure everything is stable. I will come back to your room at two o'clock.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Two o'clock. Yes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: To make sure this does not happen again, I am changing how I send notes to the pharmacy. I will now use a digital checklist that alerts me if I forget to send a message.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That sounds like a good way.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will also give you a printed list of your current medicines before you leave the hospital. You can use that list to check with your doctor at home.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I would like that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is distressing. Thank you for being so patient with me.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you, doctor.

H.justification: Resident allows patient to finish turns and adjusts pacing to distress, with no interruptions or rushing language.

E.justification: Error named explicitly in the first turn using lay language, and comprehension was checked once via teach-back.

A.justification: Direct apologies are used, but the resident dilutes accountability by citing an excuse ('We were very busy on that day').

R.justification: Resident engages emotional bids and names a specific emotion ('distressing') at the end.

T.justification: Plan includes specific steps with timelines (2 o'clock), a named patient role (throw pills in trash), and a prevention strategy (digital checklist).
